title: C# Questions & Answers - Fundamentals of Inheritance
sourceFile: Inheritance Fundamentals - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on fundamental of inheritance in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Which procedure among the following should be used to implement a 'Kind of' (is-a) relationship between two entities?
questions.explanation: An is-a / kind-of relationship is modeled with inheritance (or interface implementation). A has-a relationship is composition or aggregation, not inheritance.

questions.question: How many forms of inheritance are commonly listed in OOP (single, multilevel, hierarchical, multiple)?
questions.explanation: Textbooks often list four forms: single, multilevel, hierarchical, and multiple. C# allows only one class base (no multiple class inheritance) but a class may implement many interfaces. Inheritance depth is not limited to 4.

questions.question: What does the following C# code signify?

options.text: Declaration of base class & subclass and how subclass inherits the base class

questions.explanation: class a is the base class. class b : a declares a derived class that inherits from a.

questions.question: In an inheritance chain through which of the following, the base class and its components are accessible to the derived class?
questions.explanation: Which base members a derived class can see is controlled by access modifiers (public, protected, internal, protected internal, private protected). C# has no :: scope-resolution operator for that. The dot operator is for member access, not for opening the inheritance chain.

questions.question: Select the class visibility modifiers among the following:

options.text: Private, protected, public, internal, protected internal

questions.explanation: The usual set taught for types/members is public, private, protected, internal, and protected internal. C# 7.2 also added private protected. Nested types may be private or protected; top-level classes may not.

questions.question: In Inheritance concept, which of the following members of base class are accessible to derived class members?
questions.explanation: A derived class can use public and protected (and internal, in the same assembly) members of the base. private members are not accessible in the derived class. static is not an access level; C# has no shared keyword (that is VB).

questions.question: Wrong statement about inheritance in C# .NET?

options.text: In inheritance chain, object construction begins from base class towards derived class
Inheritance cannot extend base class functionality
A derived class object contains all base class data

questions.explanation: Inheritance is specifically a way to reuse and extend a base class. Construction does run base-then-derived, and a derived object contains the base fields, so a, c are true; b is the false statement.

questions.question: A class member declared protected becomes member of subclass of which type?
questions.explanation: A protected member stays protected in a derived class. It is visible to the subclass and to further derived types, not as public or private.

questions.question: Which of the following functionality is facilitated by inheritance mechanism?

options.text: Use the existing functionality of base class
Override the existing functionality of base class
Implements new functionality in derived class

questions.explanation: A derived class can use inherited members, override virtual ones, and add new members.

questions.question: Which statements among following are correct?

options.text: We can derive a class from a base class even if source code of base class not available
Multiple inheritance is different from multiple levels of inheritance
It is legal to make objects of one class as members of another class

questions.explanation: You can inherit from a compiled class without its source. Multiple inheritance (many bases) is not the same as multilevel (A→B→C). Nested objects are composition and are legal.

questions.question: If base class consist of two private integers, one static integer and derived class consist of two static integers and one private integer. What would be the size of derived class object?

options.text: size of object depends on sizes of its non static data members
size of a derived class object is sum of sizes of non static data members of base class and derived class
size of object is calculated using sizeof() method

questions.explanation: Instance size depends on non-static fields of the object, including those inherited from the base. Static fields live on the type, not in each instance. Option b is a reasonable description of that layout; a is the general rule. sizeof is not how you measure a class object (it applies to unmanaged types).

questions.question: Which is the correct way to prevent a class abc from being inherited?
questions.explanation: A sealed class cannot be used as a base class, so it cannot be inherited.

questions.question: Given class sample is inherited by class sample 1. Which are the correct statements about construction of object of class sample?

options.text: While creating the object firstly the constructor of class sample will be called followed by constructor of class sample 1
The constructor of only sample class will be called
While creating the object firstly constructor of class sample 1 will be called followed by constructor of class sample
The order of calling constructors depend on whether constructors in class sample and sample 1 are private or public

questions.explanation: When constructing a derived sample1 object, the base class constructor (sample) runs first, then the derived constructor (sample1).

questions.question: Which form of inheritance is not supported directly by C# .NET?
questions.explanation: C# does not allow a class to inherit from more than one class. A class may implement multiple interfaces. Single, multilevel, and hierarchical class inheritance are allowed.

questions.question: If no access modifier for a class is specified, then class accessibility is defined as?
questions.explanation: A top-level class with no access modifier is internal (visible in the same assembly). private is only the default for nested types.
